Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

RLAIF-V: Aligning MLLMs through Open-Source AI Feedback for Super GPT-4V Trustworthiness (2405.17220v1) · paper method: RLAIF-V generates candidate responses with the same model/distribution, decomposes factual response content into atomic claims, queries an open-source multimodal labeler with yes/no questions and constructs preference pairs for iterative DPO training.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

RLAIF-V: Aligning MLLMs through Open-Source AI Feedback for Super GPT-4V Trustworthiness (2405.17220v1) · paper method: RefoMB descriptions start with GPT-4V drafts merged by GPT-4, then human additions/corrections and verification by at least two graduate students; GPT-4 uses descriptions to judge response pairs against GPT-4V.

cohort3.claim.rlaifv.evaluation-human-proprietary

  • This assertion originated as an author proposal; separate review receipts determine its current status.
  • Version-specific author-reported study; experiments, raw dataset records and formal proofs were not independently reproduced or verified.
  • Open-source training feedback does not mean the complete benchmark/evaluation workflow excludes humans or proprietary models. Table 4 defines99 dev and 261 test instructions; the prose’s images wording is inconsistent.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

RLAIF-V: Aligning MLLMs through Open-Source AI Feedback for Super GPT-4V Trustworthiness (2405.17220v1) · paper method: For the 146-sample MHumanEval response-level hallucination measure in v1, Table 1 reports 50.7% for OmniLMM 12B, 29.5% after RLAIF-V, and 45.9% for the compared GPT-4V condition.

RLAIF-V: Aligning MLLMs through Open-Source AI Feedback for Super GPT-4V Trustworthiness (2405.17220v1) · paper method: The 7B setting uses LLaVA 1.5 as instruction model and LLaVA-NeXT as labeler; the 12B setting uses OmniLMM as both instruction model and labeler, with four 4k-instruction iterations described for each.
